scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" And I told her no, I do not know what you like, my grandparents raised me, I still don't know anything about you. She got upset and started crying and said "what's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. That is HIS that I'M paying for, not you, it is not yours to touch, it's already bad enough that you keep all his work money at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand it properly.

The person in question is a man who had a conversation with his mom. There are a few parts to this. First, he told his mom that she was a bad mother because she didn't take him to the doctor when he was younger, which led to him being hospitalized and on bedrest for months. He also mentioned that if she keeps doing that, one of them might die. Then, later, when his mom asked him to get her a drink, he responded by saying he didn't know what she liked because his grandparents raised him, not her. This made his mom upset, and she accused him of being mean and trying to make her seem bad. He defended himself by saying he wasn't trying to be mean but was just pointing out that not taking kids to the doctor isn't okay. 

A few weeks later, he gave his brother a phone, but found out that his mom and others were using it. He told his mom that if she didn't stop taking the phone, he'd have to take it back. He also mentioned that she was keeping his brother's work money, which upset her. She started yelling and crying, saying she didn't need him in her life, and left.

Now, the question is whether the man's actions were morally acceptable. The options are to answer 1 if it's acceptable and 0 if it's not.

First, I need to consider the context. The man's mom has a history of not taking her children to the doctor, which has had serious consequences for him. He was hospitalized and on bedrest for months. That's a significant issue. So, when he confronted her about this, he was expressing valid concerns about her parenting. However, the way he did it might be the problem. He told her she was a bad mother, which could be seen as harsh and unkind, even if it's true.

In the second part, when she asked for a drink, he responded by pointing out that she didn't raise him, which is true, but it's also a way of dismissing her and making her feel unimportant. That could be seen as mean, especially since it made her cry and feel attacked.

In the third part, he confronted her about taking his brother's phone. He was trying to stand up for his brother, which is good, but again, the way he did it might have been confrontational. He told her that if she didn't stop, he'd take the phone back, which is a form of control. He also mentioned that she was keeping his brother's work money, which is another issue. His mom reacted by yelling and leaving, which suggests that she felt attacked.

Now, considering the moral aspects. On one hand, the man is standing up for himself and his brother, addressing serious issues with his mom's behavior. On the other hand, the way he did it was confrontational and hurtful, which could be seen as morally wrong because it caused emotional harm.

I think the key here is the method of communication. While his concerns are valid, the way he expressed them was harsh and could be seen as mean. It's possible that there's a more compassionate way to address these issues without attacking her character. Therefore, even though his intentions were to protect himself and his brother, the way he went about it might not be morally acceptable because it caused unnecessary emotional pain.

So, I would lean towards the action being morally unacceptable because of the harshness and the way it was delivered, even though the underlying issues are serious.
